items.name: p-scatter-chart-14
items.title: Scatter Chart - Scatter with Jitter
items.description: When many rows share the same date (a strip plot), points stack on top of each other. Pass `jitter` to `ScatterChart` to spread them horizontally (and optionally vertically). Offsets are seeded and deterministic — no `Math.random` — so points never jump between renders or SSR/hydration. Hover snaps to the nearest jittered point, the tooltip shows the original values, and `ChartTooltip` hides its crosshair line by default (it would mark a date, not the hovered point — pass `showCrosshair` to opt back in).

items.name: p-chart-band-1
items.title: Band - Range area
items.description: A `Band` on its own is a range area chart: a filled area between a per-row low and high, with no centre line. The y-axis scales to the band, and the tooltip shows the range for the hovered date.

items.name: p-chart-band-2
items.title: Band - Range area + line combo
items.description: Use one `Band` per series and give each the same colour as its `Line` — for example each team's min / max around its average. The tooltip lists every line value and every band range for the hovered date. `strokeWidth={0}` drops the band edges so only the lines are stroked.

items.name: p-chart-band-3
items.title: Band - Band
items.description: Shade a range between two per-row values — min/max, a confidence interval, or Bollinger bands — with `Band`. Place it before your `Line`s; it reveals and morphs with them and extends the y-domain to fit both edges. Use `withBollingerBands` to derive the edges from a series.

items.name: p-chart-band-4
items.title: Band - Bollinger bands
items.description: `withBollingerBands` adds a rolling simple moving average (SMA) ± `multiplier` standard deviations to each row. Rows before the window fills get `null` for all three keys, which `Band` renders as a gap (pass `minPeriods: 1` to start at the first row instead).

items.name: p-chart-band-5
items.title: Band - Fill types
items.description: `fillType` switches between a flat `"solid"` fill, a vertical `"gradient"` (from `fillOpacity` at the upper edge to `gradientToOpacity` at the lower edge), and a `"pattern"` fill using the `Background` presets.

items.name: p-chart-band-6
items.title: Band - Faded edges
items.description: `fadeEdges` fades the fill and strokes to transparent. Horizontal fades span the plot width; vertical fades span the band's own pixel height. `fadeSize` sets how much of that width or height each fade covers.

items.name: p-chart-band-7
items.title: Band - Edge strokes
items.description: Both edges share `stroke`, `strokeWidth`, `strokeDasharray`, and `strokeOpacity`. Override one edge with `upperStroke` / `lowerStroke`, or pass `false` to hide it.

items.name: p-chart-markers-3
items.title: Markers - Simple custom marker
items.description: `ChartMarkers` always draws a circular badge. For a minimal annotation — a small diamond above the plot with a dashed guide — write your own layer with `useChart`. `xScale` maps the marker date to a pixel, and `innerHeight` is the plot height. Any SVG you return renders in the chart's plot space, so negative `y` sits in the top margin. Set the static `__isPostOverlay` flag on the component (the same flag `LineSeriesTerminalMarker` uses) so the layer renders outside the series reveal clip; otherwise the glyph above the plot top is clipped.
